title: Repeatable Adobe pipeline turning one raw exercise clip into a branded vertical coaching reel (scene summary, watermark, muscle-group callout, vertical cut)
grounding_note: VERBATIM from the real brief: a personal-training business with a library of 5,000+ exercises wants to turn raw footage into short educational exercise reference videos; the stated workflow goals quoted nearly word-for-word are reusable branding overlays / watermarks / footers, arrows/highlights/callouts pointing to muscle groups or movement patterns, and clip organization / naming conventions / metadata. The original post is a request to HIRE A COACH to architect a repeatable Premiere Pro + Claude pipeline (an abstract consulting ask, not a single deliverable). To make it a runnable Adobe-connector benchmark I REASONABLY ENRICHED it into ONE concrete instantiation of that repeatable pipeline run end-to-end on a single representative exercise ('Goblet Squat'): the agent produces the actual reusable asset set + one finished branded vertical reel, which is exactly the repeatable unit the consultant was being hired to design. The specific exercise name, the 30s/1080x1920 reel spec, the brand color/white watermark choice, and the folder/naming convention are enriched concretizations consistent with the brief; nothing contradicts it. NOTE on honesty: Premiere-class transitions, on-screen text/caption compositing, and overlaying the watermark/arrow physically onto video frames are NOT available on the Adobe connector (no video compositing) — so this benchmark targets the parts that ARE real Adobe tools: headless creation of the reusable branding+callout overlay assets, vertical reframing, an AI highlight cut, and the organized asset library; the final composite/burn-in is explicitly left as the human/Premiere step the consultant would still own.
one_line_ask: Run our repeatable exercise-reel pipeline on one raw 'Goblet Squat' clip: build the reusable white-watermark and branded muscle-group arrow overlays, reframe to vertical, cut a ~15s reference reel, and file everything under our naming convention.
full_brief:
We run a personal-training business with a library of 5,000+ exercises and want to turn raw footage into short, consistent educational reference videos for coach education and client support — today each one takes ~15s in Premiere and we want a repeatable, AI-assisted production pipeline. This task is ONE run of that pipeline on a single representative exercise, the Goblet Squat, so we can validate the repeatable unit before scaling it across the library.

Supplied assets: (1) a raw ~15s 4K landscape clip of a coach demoing the goblet squat; (2) our gym's square logo PNG (dark logo on transparent-ish background); (3) a flat hand-drawn red 'muscle-activation' arrow/callout PNG we use to point at the working muscle groups.

What we need produced this run:
1. REUSABLE WATERMARK — our logo turned into a transparent, corner-sized, white version that reads on dark gym footage (this becomes a reusable overlay asset for the whole library).
2. REUSABLE MUSCLE-GROUP CALLOUT — the hand-drawn arrow cleaned up into a crisp scalable vector recolored to our brand accent, sized as an overlay element (also reusable library-wide).
3. VERTICAL REEL — the raw clip reframed to 1080x1920 vertical (full length, no trimming at this step) and then cut down by AI into a punchy ~15s highlight 'reference reel' of the key reps.
4. ORGANIZED LIBRARY ENTRY — a folder following our naming convention (Exercise / LowerBody / GobletSquat) with the finished reel + the reusable overlay assets copied in, ready to template across the next 5,000 clips.

Honesty note for the vendor: we understand the actual frame-by-frame compositing (placing the watermark and arrow onto the video, adding on-screen text, transitions) stays in Premiere on our side — what we want from this automated pipeline is every input asset and the reframed/cut reel prepared and organized so that final Premiere step is fast and identical every time.

inputs.name: goblet_squat_raw_4k.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: Handheld documentary 4K 3840x2160 landscape clip, ~45 seconds, of a real fitness coach in a slightly worn commercial gym demonstrating a goblet squat holding a single dumbbell at the chest. Natural window + overhead fluorescent mixed lighting, visible floor rubber tiles, a rack of weights softly out of focus behind. The coach demonstrates clear, deliberate form to camera across 4-5 full reps, showing chest up, weight in the heels, and drive through the floor through visible body mechanics. Real skin texture, sweat sheen, natural body mechanics, candid not-glossy realism, no captions or graphics burned in.
inputs.realism_notes: Must be genuine handheld 4K landscape footage with clear, readable body mechanics across the reps, giving the reframe and highlight-cut steps clean, well-composed motion to work from. No on-screen text/graphics (those are produced downstream).

inputs.name: gym_logo_square.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A clean square brand logo for a personal-training gym named 'IRONLINE COACHING' — a bold geometric barbell-and-line monogram mark above the wordmark, solid dark charcoal (#1C1C1C) artwork on a flat light grey background, crisp vector-like edges, high contrast, centered, 2048x2048, no photographic texture.
inputs.realism_notes: Dark mark on light background so image_remove_background has a clean edge to cut and image_apply_color_overlay has solid dark pixels to recolor to white. Logo wordmark text must render legibly (gemini-3-pro-image for text).

inputs.name: muscle_arrow_callout_raw.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A single flat hand-drawn-style curved red arrow with a small 'GLUTES' tag at the tail, drawn with a marker texture, solid red (#D8352A) on a plain white background, slightly rough edges as if hand-drawn, 1600x1600, no other elements, no shadow.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat solid-color marker arrow on plain white so image_vectorize produces a clean SVG and image_fill_area can solid-recolor the traced shape to the brand accent. Rough hand-drawn edges justify the vectorize cleanup step.

inputs.name: coach_cue_script.json
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a small JSON object with the exercise metadata and the on-screen coaching-cue lines for a goblet squat demo: fields = exercise_name, primary_muscles (array), secondary_muscles (array), cue_lines (array of 5 short on-screen form-cue strings), naming_slug ('Exercise/LowerBody/GobletSquat'). Used only as the ground-truth reference for naming and to validate the AI summary, not edited by the connector.
inputs.realism_notes: Lightweight reference metadata so the grader can check the clip naming/metadata against ground truth; not a connector input that gets transformed.

inputs.name: raw_supplemental_02.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL handheld documentary landscape video, raw phone/camera footage (NOT a 3D render, NOT CGI, NOT animation), of a real athletic male fitness coach in a slightly worn commercial gym demonstrating a goblet squat. WIDE medium-full shot on a locked tripod: the coach's WHOLE body is visible inside the frame from the top of his head down to his knees, with clear empty headroom ABOVE his head at all times; his full face and head stay in frame for the entire clip and he looks directly at the camera and talks to it while demonstrating. The camera stays LOCKED and level and does NOT tilt down, pan, drift, zoom or crop the head out. He holds a single black hex dumbbell vertically against his chest with both hands and performs slow controlled reps, lowering until his thighs are parallel then standing tall, facing camera. He wears a PLAIN solid black crew-neck t-shirt and PLAIN heather-grey athletic joggers that are COMPLETELY BLANK: no logos, no swoosh, no tick, no brand names, no printed text, no emblems on shirt, pants or shoes. Background: racks of black rubber dumbbells softly out of focus, black rubber floor tiles, frosted windows with soft natural daylight and overhead fluorescent light. Real skin texture, light sweat sheen, natural body mechanics, candid documentary realism, subtle handheld motion. No on-screen text, captions, watermarks or graphics burned into the frame. Different camera angle: wider establishing framing, slow push-in. Realistic candid handheld raw phone/camera look. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks on any object/screen/product/clothing — plain unbranded or fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplemental raw coverage clip (10s, 1080p, silent) generated to match the primary clip's look — a different angle/beat so the edit has real, cuttable coverage rather than one short take.

outputs.name: watermark_white_corner.png
outputs.spec: Transparent PNG of the gym logo, background removed, recolored solid white, cropped/resized to a corner-badge overlay size (~400x400) — reusable library-wide watermark.

outputs.name: muscle_arrow_accent.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vectorized muscle-group callout arrow: the raw red raster arrow is first recolored to the brand accent (image_apply_color_overlay) and scaled to overlay size (image_crop_and_resize), then traced to a crisp scalable SVG (image_vectorize) as the final step — reusable library-wide overlay element.

outputs.name: goblet_squat_vertical_full.mp4
outputs.spec: Raw clip reframed to 1080x1920 vertical, full original length (no trim) via video_resize.

outputs.name: goblet_squat_reference_reel_30s.mp4
outputs.spec: ~15s AI highlight cut (video_create_quick_cut) of the vertical clip — the punchy key-reps reference reel.

outputs.name: Exercise_LowerBody_GobletSquat_folder

connector_workflow.note: Initial load: locate the three client-supplied assets (raw goblet_squat_raw_4k.mp4, gym_logo_square.png, muscle_arrow_callout_raw.png) in CC/CC-uploads scope, returning their references for the chain.
Initialize an upload session for the raw 4K clip resolved in step 1 so it is held in CC storage as a transformable media asset.
Finalize the upload session from step 2 into a stable raw-clip asset URN that the video/summary steps consume. Ingests all 5 source clips (original + supplemental coverage) for the edit.
Cut the dark gym logo off its light background (supplied in step 1) -> transparent-background logo PNG.
Recolor the transparent logo from step 5 to solid white so it reads on dark gym footage.
Crop/resize the white logo from step 6 down to a ~400x400 corner-badge overlay -> reusable watermark_white_corner.png.

Recolor the raw red hand-drawn muscle-activation arrow raster PNG (supplied in step 1) to the brand accent color — whole-image color overlay on the solid-red marker artwork, same raster recolor pattern as the logo branch (no selection needed).
Crop/resize the recolored raster arrow from step 8 to the overlay element scale (raster->raster).
Vectorize the recolored/scaled raster arrow from step 9 into a clean crisp scalable SVG as the final step -> reusable muscle_arrow_accent.svg (genuine vector deliverable emitted by vectorize).
Reframe the finalized raw 4K landscape clip to 1080x1920 vertical at full original length (no trim) -> goblet_squat_vertical_full.mp4.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: vertical_full_clip, goblet_squat_raw_4k.mp4, raw_supplemental_02.mp4, raw_supplemental_03.mp4, raw_supplemental_04.mp4, raw_supplemental_05.mp4
connector_workflow.note: AI highlight-cut the vertical full clip from step 11 to a ~15s punchy key-reps reference reel -> goblet_squat_reference_reel_~15s.mp4.
Create the naming-convention folder Exercise/LowerBody/GobletSquat (fixed naming convention) as the organized library entry, ready to hold the finished reel and reusable overlay assets.
Copy the finished reel (step 12) + reusable watermark (step 7) + reusable arrow overlay SVG (step 10) into the step-13 folder -> the templated, organized library entry.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chain. Step 1 (asset_search) is the only initial asset lookup. Steps 2->3 build raw_clip_asset from the raw 4K clip, which feeds the video branch: video_resize (10) reframes it to vertical_full_clip, and video_create_quick_cut (11) consumes that vertical clip for the ~15s reference reel. The watermark branch chains from the logo found in step 1: image_remove_background (4) -> image_apply_color_overlay (5) -> image_crop_and_resize (6) = watermark_white_corner. The callout branch stays entirely raster until the end: from the arrow found in step 1, image_apply_color_overlay (7) recolors the raw red raster to the brand accent -> image_crop_and_resize (8) scales it -> image_vectorize (9) traces it to the final brand-accent SVG (vectorize runs LAST so muscle_arrow_accent.svg is genuinely emitted as vector and no raster-only tool ever receives an SVG). The organization branch: asset_create_folders (12) stands up the fixed naming-convention folder Exercise/LowerBody/GobletSquat, then asset_copy_assets (13) consumes the finished reel (11), the watermark (6), the arrow SVG (9) and the folder (12) to assemble the templated library entry. Every step after step 1 consumes at least one prior step's named output; the deliverable set (watermark, vector arrow, vertical clip, reference reel, organized folder) emerges only at the end of the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon and wide-mix: 13 connector calls, 11 distinct Adobe tools spanning multiple tool groups (asset/storage, media video [A], raster image [C], and the vectorize path), with three parallel sub-chains (media/reframe, watermark, callout) that converge into one organized library deliverable. It exercises real cross-group dependency tracking (the raw_clip_asset fan-out, the 4-input final copy) and forces correct execution-mode handling — the [A] async video steps interleave with [C] headless image steps. It is honestly bounded: it deliberately stops at asset preparation + reframe + AI cut + organization and explicitly leaves frame-by-frame burn-in/compositing/transitions to the human Premiere step, since Adobe-connector video compositing, on-screen text burn-in, and overlay placement are not available — making the difficulty come from orchestration and faithful capability mapping rather than from any disallowed generative/compositing shortcut.

reverify.banned_capability_check: No banned capability anywhere in the chain: no generative-expand/outpaint, no upscale/super-resolution, no text-to-image, no from-scratch art/logo, no object-removal-with-reconstruction, no video compositing/on-screen-text burn-in/overlay placement (those are explicitly left to the human Premiere step). image_apply_color_overlay is used as a whole-image tonal recolor on solid-color raster artwork (logo and arrow) — an allowed use. video_resize is full-length (no trim); video_create_quick_cut is correctly tagged async [A] and product-doable. Every tool acts on a compatible input type.
reverify.notes: Vector-branch type mismatch resolved: the arrow branch performs all raster edits (image_apply_color_overlay recolor, image_crop_and_resize scale) on the raster PNG and runs image_vectorize LAST, so no raster-only tool receives an SVG and the muscle_arrow_accent.svg deliverable is truly produced as vector by vectorize. The former missing-selection issue is gone because image_fill_area was removed entirely (recoloring is now done by whole-image color_overlay, which needs no selection). All 13 calls use real Adobe-connector tools on compatible inputs; the scene-summary deliverable was descoped (no producing step remained for it, and the summary is not load-bearing for the reusable-asset + reel + library deliverables); every declared input (raw 4K clip, square logo PNG, hand-drawn arrow PNG) is consumed by a step and declared in inputs[]. Grounding/scope unchanged and honest.
